subject: A quick question from a lazy person. do you use the alpha scaling d=1.7 when estimating theta?

messages.author: 7636027d6c15836f
messages.subject: A quick question from a lazy person. do you use the alpha scaling d=1.7 when estimating theta?
parts:
I am asking this question primarily because I am lazy to look your source code so I will not be offended in any way if you don't answer. And I am grateful that you answered several previous questions of mine.

I was wondering if you are using the a scaling constant d=1.7 when you estimate theta for producing scores for items using the coefficients of item characteristic curves. As I understand it doesn't matter if the method is MAP ML EAP or EAPsum. In all of these cases you may decide either to use this constant or not use it at all.

As I understand use of this constant is not mandatory however it changes the theta estimate for each question.

# Just to be more specific the function bellow does not have constant 1.7
res<-(exp(a*(theta-b))/(1+exp(a*(theta-b))))
# The function below has it
d<-1.7
res<-(exp(d*a*(theta-b))/(1+exp(d*a*(theta-b))))







Which function would you prefer to implement and which one did you use in mirt?


In any case thank you for the package you can't imagine how much time you saved me.
